newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Gujral retains all but five ministers.
newsitem.headline: India's Gujral retains all but five ministers.

text.p: India's new prime minister, Inder Kumar Gujral, retained the cabinet of his predecessor, H.D. Deve Gowda, except for five departing ministers, government officials said on Monday.
The returning ministers will keep the same portfolios, Gujral told reporters after taking the oath of office.
Gujral said he would remain foreign minister and also take the finance ministry portfolio.

Outgoing finance minister P. Chidambaram was not included in the 35-member cabinet as his regional Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) party decided not to join the government after its leader, G.K. Moopanar, was passed over as United Front head.
Other cabinet ministers in the outgoing government who were not included in Gujral's council of ministers were Devendra Prasad Yadav (food) and M. Arunachalam (labour).
The two junior ministers who were not retained were R. Dhanushkodi Athithan (human resource development) and S.R. Balasubramanian (personnel).
All except Devendra Prasad Yadav, who belongs to Gujral's Janata Dal party, are in the TMC. There was no immediate explanation why Devendra Prasad Yadav was not in the new cabinet.
